body:
## Summary
The foundation PR commits the real `.ai/` tree and, in the same PR, a SKILL.md that contains a verbatim second copy of every one of those files (`src/lib/standard/index.ts:57`, `src/lib/onboarding/skill.ts:117`). The doctor body alone is about 30KB of that copy.

## Description
`buildFoundation` is `[...buildStandardFiles(report), buildOnboardingSkillFile(report)]` (`src/lib/standard/index.ts:57`), and the skill it appends renders Step 0 by fencing each of those same `GeneratedFile.body` values in full (`src/lib/onboarding/skill.ts:274`, `src/lib/onboarding/skill.ts:259-270`). `/api/report/foundation/pr` passes that list straight to the committer (`src/app/api/report/foundation/pr/route.ts:68`, `src/lib/standard/pr.ts:62-76`), so an adopting repo receives `.ai/doctor.mjs` twice: once as the file its pre-push hook runs, once as text inside an always-loadable instruction file.

The embedding is correct for exactly one lane: the plain markdown download, where the repo has no files and its agent must transcribe them. In the PR lane it buys nothing and costs three things. First, a second authority for every generated fact: the registry technique `pointers-not-embeds` (repo-manifest-standard) states that an embedded copy drifts from the day it is written, and this repo preaches the same principle to its customers (`src/lib/standard/types.ts:8`, `src/lib/standard/spec.ts:54`) while its generator breaks it. Second, the copy is unmarked: the standard's `guidance` block exists precisely so a projection carries its source hash and a hand edit is diagnosable as a fail rather than invisible (`src/lib/standard/spec.ts:136-138`), yet the whole `.ai/` tree is projected into SKILL.md with no hash at all. Third, size: `line-earning` and `single-source-topology` (agent-instruction-files) both hold that an always-loaded instruction file which outgrows its budget stops being followed, and this one is roughly 65KB of embedded bodies before any prose.

Fixed looks like `renderStep0(files, mode)`. In reference mode (the PR lane) Step 0 is the file list: each path, its purpose and a `sha256` stamp, derived from `buildStandardFiles` so the list cannot go stale, plus the instruction to read the files already in the PR. In embed mode (the download) every body stays verbatim and gains the same provenance stamp per block, so a transcribed copy is comparable to its source the way a guidance projection is.

## Flow
- Extract the Step 0 renderer out of `skill.ts` into `src/lib/onboarding/step0.ts` with no behaviour change, pinned by the existing fence-escaping case.
- Add the provenance stamp to embed mode: one line per block, `sha256(f.body).slice(0,12)`, reusing the header shape `.ai/maintain.mjs project` already writes.
- Add reference mode: a table of path, purpose and hash derived from the passed `files`, the read-the-files-in-this-PR instruction, and the origin-only recovery link.
- Thread the mode: `buildOnboardingSkillFile(report, opts, mode)` and `buildFoundation` pass reference; every other caller defaults to embed.
- Add `step0.test.ts` with the acceptance cases, declare both new files in `context-map.json`, and update the two coupled docs.

## Expected impact
An adopting maintainer reviewing the foundation PR sees a reviewable SKILL.md instead of a 90KB wall, and the repo stops carrying two sources of truth for its own doctor; measured as the byte ratio between the PR-lane skill and the embed-lane skill (target under 30%) and by the new derived-path-list test. What could break: a repo whose PR lands with some files skipped (a pre-existing `CONTEXT.md`, an existing workflow) now reads Step 0 as a pointer to a file it does not have, which is why reference mode must name the recovery download and why the skipped-path case stays in the acceptance set.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the generated foundation has one authority per generated file, and the instruction file shrinks to a size an agent will actually read.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - the acceptance cases as tests in `src/lib/onboarding/step0.test.ts`, red before, green after; the byte-ratio and derived-path-list cases assert on the emitted markdown text, not on the generator internals.
Result: better
Gate: architecture

## Summary
`node .ai/doctor.mjs` prints every finding in the order the script happened to add it, with no severity grouping, no check ids and no remediation (`src/lib/standard/doctor.ts:379`). The one surface where the shift-left promise reaches a human reads as a wall.

## Description
The generated doctor is the product's primary human-facing artefact: it runs in the adopting repo's pre-push hook and on its merge gate, and its stdout is what a maintainer and that repo's own agent act on. Today the whole report is one loop (`src/lib/standard/doctor.ts:379`) over `findings` in emission order, prefixed only by a four-state icon (`src/lib/standard/doctor.ts:377`). On a fresh install the findings that block the merge are interleaved with a dozen passes, the reader is given no next action, and the stable check id that the spec presents as the way to follow a clause across runs (`src/lib/standard/spec.ts:248`) is carried in the payload (`src/lib/standard/doctor.ts:53`, `src/lib/standard/doctor.ts:404`) and withheld from the person at the terminal. There is no `--verbose`, so there is no way to quiet the passes either.

This is `finding-severity-ladder` territory (conformance-checking): the severities are in the data and are discarded at the point of presentation. The fix also answers `rule-registry-enumerated-fixtures` from the same subject, because the remediation coverage is enumerated from the declared id vocabulary rather than guessed.

Fixed looks like three blocks and a tail. FAIL first, each line as `FAIL  <check-id>  <message>` followed by a `fix:` line; then WARN the same way; then an unchecked block that keeps its reason text; then one collapsed pass line (`23 checks passed`, expanded by `--verbose`); then a Next block naming at most three actions in severity order, each quoting its check id so the reader can look the clause up in the org control matrix. The `--json` payload, the score arithmetic and the exit code are untouched, so every adopter's gate behaves exactly as before.

## Flow
- Give `add()` an optional fourth argument, `fix`, and move the remediation text already buried inside some messages (`run: node .ai/maintain.mjs project`, `Wire it in.`) into it.
- Fill a `fix` for every id in the declared vocabulary; `src/lib/standard/check-ids.ts` is the checklist, so coverage is enumerable rather than a guess.
- Replace the print loop with the grouped readout plus the collapsed pass line and `--verbose`.
- Add the Next block (at most three, severity-ordered, id-quoting) above the existing Conformance summary line, which keeps its exact shape.
- Add `src/lib/standard/doctor-readout.test.ts` on the existing execute-in-a-temp-repo harness, update the two stdout assertions in `standard.test.ts`, then add the additive spec section and re-mirror `SPEC_MD` without touching the header version.

## Expected impact
Every maintainer who adopts the standard, and every agent that runs the doctor for them, gets a verdict ordered by what blocks them plus the command to run next; measured by the acceptance cases and by the share of the declared id vocabulary that carries a fix hint (target: all of it). What could break: adopters or scripts that grep the old flat stdout, which is why the summary line's shape and the whole `--json` contract are pinned unchanged in the acceptance set.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the conformance run becomes a triaged plan a human can act on without re-reading the spec, with no change to the machine contract.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases as tests that execute the generated `.ai/doctor.mjs` against fixture repos and assert on its stdout text, red before, green after; the vocabulary-coverage case pins the emitted output against this repo's own declaration in `check-ids.ts`.
Result: better
Gate: contract

## Summary
The executive briefing's period delta, and the `value realized this period` points figure built from it, are `mean(current fleet) - mean(baseline fleet)` (`src/lib/org/briefing.ts:414`, `:440`). The cohort-matched movement they should be is already computed on the same rollup object (`src/lib/db/org-rollup.ts:437`) and already read by the Overview tab and the weekly digest.

## Description
`buildExecBriefing` receives one `OrgRollup`. That object carries `baseline` (a population snapshot) and `movement: CohortMovement | null` - movement measured only over repos present on BOTH sides of the window, with `cohortSize`, `onboarded` and `departed` beside it (`src/lib/db/org-rollup.ts:480`-`:490`). The briefing reads `baseline` and ignores `movement`: `periodDelta` (`src/lib/org/briefing.ts:414`) and `valueRealized.pointsMoved` (`src/lib/org/briefing.ts:440`) are both `rollup.avgOverall - rollup.baseline.avgOverall`, and `priorPeriod.dOverall` (`src/lib/org/briefing.ts:374`) differences two independently-populated windows.

That sum folds two independent effects into one number labelled as movement. Onboard five low-scoring repositories mid-quarter and the board PDF reports a fleet that slipped by an amount no repository experienced; onboard strong ones and it reports a climb nobody earned. The rollup's own comment says so in as many words (`src/lib/db/org-rollup.ts:494`).

This violates `analytics-time-windows` / `cohort-matched-comparison` (golden path `knowledge/software-engineering/engineering-assessment/measurement-method/analytics-time-windows/`): movement is measured only over entities present on both sides, composition is reported as its own figure, and the cohort size travels with the delta. It also trips that technique's loudest smell - "a headline delta and a movers list that disagree" - on one screen: `OrgMovers.comparedRepos` deliberately excludes onboarded repos (`src/lib/db/org-insights.ts:290`), so `BriefingMovementCard` can show zero regressions directly under a negative headline. And it breaches `baseline-as-window-start`'s "reconciling two surfaces that disagree about a delta": Overview (`src/features/standing/overview/overviewStanding.ts:88`) and the digest (`src/app/api/cron/digest/route.ts:281`) print the cohort-matched figure for the same window, so the two tabs disagree and the board-facing one is the wrong one.

Fixed looks like: `periodDelta` and `pointsMoved` come from `rollup.movement`; a new `periodMovement` block carries `cohortSize`/`onboarded`/`departed` onto `ExecBriefing`; one composer in `src/lib/org/briefingMovement.ts` writes the delta caption that the tile, the PDF, the markdown and the share page all render, so the denominator cannot be dropped on one of the four; and `briefingFigureDigest` covers the new fields so a share link cannot claim the figures are unchanged over a re-based delta.

## Flow
- Add `periodMovement: CohortMovement | null` to `ExecBriefing`; set it from `rollup.movement`, and re-point `periodDelta` + `valueRealized.pointsMoved` at `rollup.movement.overall` (null when `movement` is null).
- Write `src/lib/org/briefingMovement.ts`: `periodDeltaCaption(b)` (cohort size, plus the composition clause only when onboarded/departed are non-zero) and the null contract. Re-export from `briefing-format`'s barrel so no call site moves.
- Render the caption in the four surfaces: `BriefingTiles` via a new co-located `BriefingDeltaCaption.tsx` (briefingCards.tsx is at 198 of its 200-LOC cap, so the caption must be an extraction, not an append), `briefing-document.tsx`, `briefing-markdown.ts`, and the share page.
- Extend `briefingFigureDigest`'s projection with `cohortSize`/`onboarded`/`departed`.
- Relabel `PriorPeriodGrid` when `prior.realScoredCount !== briefing.realScoredCount`: a difference of two population means is a standing comparison with two denominators, never movement.
- Write the acceptance cases as tests in `briefing.test.ts` and `briefingCards.dom.test.tsx` (red first), including the Overview-vs-briefing reconciliation case.
- Update `docs/features/org-planning/plan.md`, deleting any stated gap this closes.

## Expected impact
Everyone who reads a board artifact: the PDF, the Briefing tab and the public share link stop reporting onboarding as score movement, and the Briefing tab stops contradicting Overview and the weekly digest over the same window. Measured by the reconciliation test (one rollup fixture, two surfaces, one number) and by the composition fixture whose delta is 0 today and negative. What could break: already-issued share tokens will report "figures moved" on their next open, because the fingerprint's projection changed - loud, one-time, and the safe direction.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the briefing's headline movement figure becomes movement, carries its denominator, and agrees with the two other surfaces that already compute it correctly.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases as vitest cases in `src/lib/org/briefing.test.ts` and `briefingCards.dom.test.tsx`, red before, green after
Result: better
Gate: contract

title: Issued briefing links: an inventory an owner can revoke from, not an API nobody reaches
acceptance: Owner on the Briefing tab, GET /api/org/briefing/share returns two grants -> both render newest-first with minted-at, minting owner, scope (whole org / segment / stack), frozen window, expiry, and open count. Today no surface in src/ calls that endpoint at all.

Revoke on a live grant -> POST /api/org/briefing/share/revoke { org, jti }; on 200 that row re-renders as Revoked with no Revoke control, without a page reload or a second GET being required for correctness.
A revoked grant and an expired grant render DIFFERENT status words and neither offers Revoke; a grant whose mint row recorded no expiry is never shown as expired.
opens === 0 -> 'not opened yet'; opens > 0 -> 'opened N times, last <lastOpenedAt>'. Never a bare '0 opens' presented as a healthy state.
Non-owner viewer (canShare false) -> the inventory does not mount and no request is issued to /api/org/briefing/share.
GET fails (503 or network) -> the panel says the inventory could not be read and does NOT render the 'no links issued' empty state; the manual revoke-by-id field stays enabled.

The panel states that the list is bounded by audit retention and is not the enforcement point, and accepts a pasted link id so a grant older than retention (absent from the list) can still be revoked - the revoke endpoint deliberately does not require the grant to be listed.
A link minted by the Share button appears in the list immediately on success (the mint response's jti/expiresAt is prepended), so the URL that today exists only in the clipboard has a durable home.

## Summary
An owner can mint a public briefing link but cannot see or kill one. `GET /api/org/briefing/share` (`src/app/api/org/briefing/share/route.ts:33`) and `POST /api/org/briefing/share/revoke` (`src/app/api/org/briefing/share/revoke/route.ts:34`) are fully built, owner-gated and tested, and no file under `src/` outside their own tests calls either.

## Description
The Briefing tab's sharing affordance is one button (`src/features/bought/executive/ExecutiveTabActions.tsx:51`), which POSTs a mint and copies the URL to the clipboard (`BriefingShareButton.tsx:39`). Its own comment records what happens next: "Each mint is a live 7-day token; losing the URL forces a re-mint" (`BriefingShareButton.tsx:31`). So the only record of a published fleet-posture document is in whatever the owner pasted it into, and the only way to retire one is the blunt lever the data layer explicitly set out to replace - demote the minter, killing every link they ever issued (`src/lib/briefing-share.ts:9`-`:13`).

Everything needed is already in place and reaches nobody. `BriefingShareGrant` carries jti, minted-at, minter, expiry, frozen window, segment and stack scope, revoked, expired, opens and lastOpenedAt (`src/lib/db/org-share.ts:125`-`:148`). `revokedBriefingShareJtis` was written as a batched fail-closed set lookup "because the list view asks about every grant on the page at once" (`src/lib/db/org-share.ts:100`-`:107`) - for a list view that was never built. `briefing.share.minted` / `.opened` / `.revoked` are already registered audit actions (`src/features/admin/audit/auditActions.ts:96`-`:100`). The retention caveat that a reader most needs - the list is an inventory, not the enforcement point (`src/lib/db/org-share.ts:166`) - is a comment in the db layer.

This is the state the registry's `executive-reporting` / `expiring-share-links` technique governs (`use_when: revoking access to a distributed snapshot`): a surface that reports state the user must be able to act on, where today it reports nothing at all. The repo has already built the whole mechanism of that technique (jti identity, permanent ledger, fail-closed read, open logging); the one missing piece is the human end of it.

Fixed looks like a `Share links` panel on the Briefing tab, owner-only: one row per grant with its scope, frozen window, expiry, open count and last open, a Revoke button that POSTs the jti and re-renders the row, an explicit paste-an-id field so a grant aged out of audit retention can still be killed, and a line that says plainly what the list is bounded by. The mint button prepends its new grant on success, which also gives the link URL a durable home instead of only a clipboard.

## Flow
- `shareLinkRows.ts` (pure): `BriefingShareGrant[]` -> rows with a single `status` of live | expired | revoked and the opens phrasing (`not opened yet` vs `opened N times, last <date>`), so absence never renders as a zero.
- `useShareLinks.ts` (client hook): GET on mount with a limit, POST revoke, optimistic row status with rollback on failure, and a distinct error state for `could not read` separate from `none issued`.
- `ShareLinkInventory.tsx` (client): the table, the Revoke control, the revoke-by-id field, and the retention note. Each new file stays under the 200-LOC `src/features/**` cap.
- Mount it from `ExecutiveTab.v1.tsx` and `ExecutiveTab.v2.tsx` under the existing `canShare` flag (already `briefingShareEnabled() && isOwner`, `ExecutiveTab.tsx:47`), and lift the mint result into the hook from `BriefingShareButton`.
- Write `shareLinkRows.test.ts` and `ShareLinkInventory.dom.test.tsx` from the acceptance cases, red first.
- Update `docs/features/org-planning/plan.md`, deleting any stated gap about share links being unlistable.

## Expected impact
Org owners: the question "which of our board links are live, who sent them, what scope, and has anyone opened them" becomes a glance instead of unanswerable, and killing one leaked link stops requiring a curl. Measured by the acceptance tests and by `briefing.share.revoked` rows appearing from a UI actor rather than never. What could break: the panel issues one extra owner-gated GET per Briefing render, and the fail-closed revocation lookup means an unreachable ledger shows every grant as revoked - the panel must label that as an unreadable ledger, which acceptance case 6 pins.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an owner can see and retire every briefing link their org has published, from the tab that publishes them.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases as vitest cases in `shareLinkRows.test.ts` and `ShareLinkInventory.dom.test.tsx`, red before, green after
Result: better
Gate: none

acceptance: coalesceScan: the last waiter's signal aborts -> the shared AbortSignal is NOT aborted and the entry stays in the map; inflightScanCount() is still 1 immediately after release.

coalesceScan: a new caller for the same key arrives inside the linger window -> onJoin fires, the last progress frame is replayed to its sink, the factory runs exactly once, and both callers resolve to the same report.
coalesceScan: no caller arrives inside the linger window -> the shared signal aborts once the window expires and inflightScanCount() returns 0 (no leaked entry, no runaway run).

scanResume: an anchor written for acme/web with no ref or subPath reads back live inside the TTL; the same anchor does not match the subject acme/web with ref=feat; an anchor older than scanClientTimeoutMs() reads as expired; a storage accessor that throws reads as no anchor.

useReportScan: a joined SSE frame sets resumed=true, and the anchor is cleared once the scan settles (done or error) so the next visit cannot claim a rejoin.

Loading with resumed=true renders a named restored-work line (the repo plus elapsed-since-start) and a Start a fresh scan control that clears the anchor and re-runs with fresh=1; with resumed=false neither appears.

stream route: two sequential POSTs for the same uncached commit, the first disconnected mid-scan and the second opened inside the linger window -> scanRepository is called once, the second connection receives the result frame, and its quota slot is refunded (joinedInflight).

## Summary
A live scan on /report?repo= is owned by one browser connection: useReportScan's cleanup aborts it (src/components/report/useReportScan.ts:389) and the stream route aborts the ingest plus the LLM on that disconnect (src/app/api/scan/stream/route.ts:285). Reload the page four minutes into a six-minute scan and the whole run is discarded, even though the server already has the machinery to let a second connection join it.

## Description
coalesceScan (src/lib/cache.ts:217) coalesces concurrent scans of the same cache key onto one run, refcounts the abort so one disconnect cannot kill a run others want, fans the owner's progress frames out to every listener (src/lib/cache.ts:292) and replays the last frame to a late joiner (src/lib/cache.ts:316). The stream route even carries the user-facing copy for it (src/app/api/scan/stream/route.ts:305). None of it is reachable from a reload, because the refcount is released synchronously and the abort fires the moment it reaches zero (src/lib/cache.ts:332) - and a reload closes the old connection strictly before the new request arrives, so the refcount always passes through zero. The in-flight entry is gone before the returning tab can ask for it.

The client side has the matching hole: nothing durable records that a scan was started for this subject. On remount the hook treats the page as a cold first load, peeks the cache (which cannot hit, because the report was never persisted), and starts a second full ingest plus LLM completion. At the measured claude-cli median of 360s (src/components/report/scanEstimate.ts:21) that is six minutes of wall clock and a second inference bill for a page refresh.

This is session-resume (knowledge/software-engineering/ui-surfaces/shell-and-navigation/session-resume/session-resume.md) and specifically its resume-affordances technique: a session that ended without the user's intent, and the user arriving at the work's own home by their own choice, are the two cases where in-progress work restores itself rather than being offered, and the restored work carries a visible start-over control. A reload of the scan's own URL is both of those cases at once.

Fixed looks like: the server keeps a settled-to-zero in-flight entry alive for a bounded linger window instead of aborting it, so a returning connection joins the run already under way; the client keeps a short-lived anchor naming the scan subject it started, so on remount it goes straight to the stream, is told by an explicit joined frame that it rejoined, and says so with a start-over exit. The linger also means a run nobody is watching still finishes and persists, so an abandoned scan produces the permalink instead of producing nothing.

## Flow
- Add a linger constant and a deferred abort to coalesceScan in src/lib/cache.ts: on release at zero waiters, schedule the abort; a joiner inside the window cancels the timer and attaches; expiry aborts and evicts. Keep the aborted-entry guard (src/lib/cache.ts:269) so a post-window caller starts fresh.
- Pin the new behaviour in src/lib/cache.test.ts with fake timers: join inside the window, abort-and-evict at expiry, fresh computation after it.
- New pure module src/components/report/scanResume.ts: write, read and expire an anchor keyed on the exact scan subject (repo, fresh, ref, subPath), TTL = scanClientTimeoutMs(), over an injected storage-like interface so every branch is unit-testable and a throwing accessor degrades to no anchor.
- Thread it through src/components/report/useReportScan.ts: write at scan start, clear on settle, and skip the peek when a live anchor matches this subject.
- Emit an explicit joined SSE frame from src/app/api/scan/stream/route.ts beside the existing progress copy, and map it in the hook to resumed=true (a message-string match is not a contract).
- Render the restored state in src/components/report/ReportClientStatus.tsx: a named line plus a Start a fresh scan control; pass resumed through src/components/report/ReportClient.tsx.
- Update docs/features/scanning/scan.md: the linger window, the rejoin, and what a reload now costs.

## Expected impact
Anyone who reloads, follows a link away, or is navigated off mid-scan - the longest wait in the product - comes back to the scan still running instead of starting over, and an abandoned scan now finishes and persists so the permalink resolves for the next visitor. Measured by the acceptance cases plus a scanRepository call count of exactly one across a disconnect-then-reconnect pair in the route test. What could break: a lingering run keeps burning inference for up to the window with nobody watching, so the window must stay short enough that an abandoned scan is a bounded cost, and the route's post-await send on a closed controller must stay swallowed.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a multi-minute scan survives the loss of the connection that started it, with no duplicate inference.
Before: 0 of 9 acceptance cases pass
After: 9 of 9
Method: gate - the acceptance cases written as tests in src/lib/cache.test.ts, src/components/report/scanResume.test.ts, src/components/report/useReportScan.dom.test.tsx and src/app/api/scan/stream/route.test.ts, red before, green after
Result: better
Gate: architecture

## Summary
The report's only freshness signal is one muted relative-time string (src/components/report/FreshnessControl.tsx:70), identical for a reading taken ten minutes ago and one taken seven months ago, and it never says that the repo has moved off the commit that was scored - even though the product already declares a 7-day belief window (src/lib/scan-cache.ts:28) and already stores both shas.

## Description
freshness() (src/lib/ui.ts:228) is a pure relative-time formatter: no tiering, no threshold, no tone change, and past 24 hours it hands off to timeAgo (src/lib/ui.ts:238) and still renders text-slate-500. The scan pipeline, meanwhile, holds a precise opinion about when a reading stops counting: scanMaxCacheAgeMs() defaults to 7 days and src/lib/scan-cache.ts:158 refuses to serve a persisted report past it as current. The permalink serves such a report anyway - it is the pinned artifact - and the surface says nothing. The second missing fact is drift: Scan.headSha records the commit scored (prisma/schema.prisma:589) and Repository.headSha records the head last seen (prisma/schema.prisma:310), so a scored-abc1234-last-seen-def5678 clause is two columns away, through an existing exported reader (getHeadHint, src/lib/db/scans-read.ts:241) that costs no GitHub call and already degrades to null on a DB blip.

The claim travels further than the page. generateMetadata asserts the score with no date (src/app/report/[owner]/[repo]/page.tsx:73), and the unfurl artwork carries no scan date at all (grepping scannedAt in src/lib/og/report-card.tsx returns nothing), so a Slack or GitHub unfurl of a stale reading presents a score as a present-tense fact about the repo. That is public-claim-provenance's degraded-never-claims-live (knowledge/software-engineering/ui-surfaces/published-surfaces/public-claim-provenance/public-claim-provenance.md) and the four-state discipline of content-freshness-states in session-resume: every state renders, and no state is allowed to wear the fresh costume.

Fixed looks like a small pure state machine - current, aging, stale, unknown, with an orthogonal drifted flag - deriving its thresholds from scanMaxCacheAgeMs() so one knob governs the pipeline and the label; the control then states the tier, states the drift in the honest last-seen wording Repository.headSha actually supports, and promotes the Re-test affordance that already exists rather than adding a second button. The reader stops having to guess whether to trust the number, because the page finally tells them what it is a claim about.

## Flow
- New pure module src/components/report/reportFreshness.ts: reportFreshnessState({ scannedAt, scoredSha, lastSeenHead, now }) returning a tier, a drifted flag and a reason, thresholds derived from scanMaxCacheAgeMs(), every branch total over null and garbled input.
- Pin it in src/components/report/reportFreshness.test.ts - the cases above, including the null-lastSeenHead and unparseable-date branches.
- Render it in src/components/report/FreshnessControl.tsx: tier tone and stated reason on the existing row, a drift clause below, Re-test promoted when the state is stale or drifted. The file is 104 lines today; if the drift clause pushes it, extract a co-located FreshnessReason.tsx sibling (the 300-LOC cap applies here, not the 200).
- Thread lastSeenHead from src/app/report/[owner]/[repo]/page.tsx (add getHeadHint to the existing Promise.all at line 154) through ReportView and ReportHeader as one optional prop, so the live-scan path with no prop renders exactly today's output.
- Add the date to generateMetadata's description for a stale reading, and print the scan date on the share-card artwork in src/lib/og/report-card.tsx (which also fixes the downloadable card).
- New src/app/report/[owner]/[repo]/page.freshness.test.tsx for the metadata case; update docs/features/reporting/report.md with the four states and the drift wording.

## Expected impact
Every reader of a shared report permalink - the product's most-linked URL - learns in the masthead whether the number is about the repo as it is now, and an unfurl stops making a dateless present-tense claim. Measured by the acceptance cases, and observably by the share of Re-tests that start from a stale or drifted state instead of from a blind click. What could break: Repository.headSha is a remembered hint, so an over-eager drifted claim on a repo whose hint was refreshed by an unrelated path would be noise - which is exactly why the copy says last seen head and the clause is suppressed when the hint is null.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a published score states what it is a claim about, in tiers derived from the belief window the pipeline already enforces.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases as tests in src/components/report/reportFreshness.test.ts, src/components/report/FreshnessControl.test.tsx and src/app/report/[owner]/[repo]/page.freshness.test.tsx, red before, green after
Result: better
Gate: contract

title: Segments keep a rule, not a snapshot: declared membership with owned rows and visible drift
acceptance: POST /api/org/segments/<id>/rule { kind: "language", values: ["Python"] } from a member of the owning org -> 200 and the segment carries the rule; GET /api/org/segments?org=<slug> returns `rule` on that SegmentRow. The same POST for a segment id owned by ANOTHER org -> 404 (resolve-then-gate through getSegmentOrgSlug, never a caller-supplied org beside a caller-supplied id).

Apply the rule { kind: "language", values: ["Python"] } on an org with 5 Python repos in the taggable universe -> 5 RepoSegment rows exist with source "rule" and the response is { added: 5, removed: 0 }; applying it again -> { added: 0, removed: 0 } and no row is rewritten (idempotent).

A repo tagged by hand into a ruled segment whose language does NOT match the rule SURVIVES an apply (source "manual" is never reaped); a rule-owned row whose repo primaryLanguage has since changed to Go IS removed by the same apply. Both assertions in one test so the ownership split cannot regress to last-write-wins.

## Summary
A segment's membership is a hand-maintained snapshot. The "auto-add by language or team" control (src/features/standing/repositories/RepoSegmentsPanel.autoAdd.ts:48) computes the match set in the browser, bulk-tags it once, and persists nothing about the intent, so `Segment` (prisma/schema.prisma:401) has no idea it was ever meant to be "all Python repos" and never converges again.

## Description
Today the declared thing and the stored thing are the same list. A user picks "Python" and a segment, the client filters its own props (src/features/standing/repositories/RepoSegmentsPanel.autoAdd.ts:48) and POSTs the names to setRepoSegmentsBulk (src/lib/db/segments.ts:187), which writes membership rows that carry no provenance (prisma/schema.prisma:417). From that second on the segment is a frozen photograph of a predicate: a repo onboarded tomorrow with that language never joins, a repo whose primaryLanguage flips never leaves, and a team segment goes stale on every GitHub team change. Nothing on screen says so.

That silence is the defect, because the stale set is load-bearing downstream. Each segment card mounts SegmentActions over its tagged slice (src/features/standing/repositories/SegmentCard.tsx:56), and those controls set autoscan cadence and scan "just this segment" (src/features/standing/repositories/SegmentActions.tsx:3) - so drift spends credits on the wrong repos and quietly omits the new ones. The same tag set scopes every `?segment=` reading on the Overview through getOrgRollup's segmentScope.

The registry calls this a convergence loop, not a bulk write. Resolved through ../ai-registry/knowledge/software-engineering/index.json: `convergence-loop-and-requeue` (operations/control-plane-operations) governs a loop that drives observed reality toward a DECLARED record, which is precisely what is missing - there is a declaration in the user's head and no record of it. `declarative-resource-lifecycle`'s technique `per-field-write-ownership` supplies the second half and the real design decision: once two writers (a human tagging by hand, a rule converging) touch one join table, last-write-wins is the absence of a policy, and the symptom is "a value is set, something restores it a minute later, and nothing records who did it". So a membership row gains an owner (`source`: manual | rule), convergence may only reap rows it owns, and a hand-tag is permanent against the rule.

Fixed looks like: `Segment.ruleJson` holds an optional declaration ({ kind: "language" | "team", values: string[] }); `segmentDrift` is a pure function over the taggable repos the Segments view ALREADY has in hand (src/features/standing/repositories/SegmentsSection.tsx:65, fed by src/lib/db/segments.ts:261) so the drift line costs no query; and convergence is an explicit, audited apply. The posture copies reconcileListedRepos (src/lib/db/org-watch.ts:717), which marks drift and leaves the remedy to the user rather than mutating the fleet behind their back - the conservative choice that keeps this card's risk at 6 instead of 8.

## Flow
- Add `Segment.ruleJson String?` and `RepoSegment.source String @default("manual")` to prisma/schema.prisma plus a hand-written migration dir (the house pattern under prisma/migrations/).
- Write src/lib/org/segmentRule.ts: the rule type, a parse/validate that returns a human error like segmentInputError (src/lib/db/segments.ts:48), `matchesRule(repo, rule)` over TaggableRepo, and the pure `segmentDrift({ rule, repos, membership })` returning { toAdd, toRemove } or null for an unruled segment. Unit-test it first - every acceptance case 2-4 is red here before any DB work.
- Teach src/lib/db/segments.ts: carry `rule` on SegmentRow, accept it on create/update, make setRepoSegmentsBulk stamp `source`, and add `applySegmentRule(orgSlug, segmentId)` that adds matches as rule-owned and deletes ONLY rule-owned non-matches, in one transaction, returning { added, removed }.
- Add /api/org/segments/[id]/rule/route.ts: PUT sets the rule, POST applies it. Resolve the org from the row (getSegmentOrgSlug, src/lib/db/segments.ts:139) then gate, exactly as /api/org/segments/[id]/route.ts:17 does, so src/app/api/org/id-routes-gated.test.ts keeps passing. Audit `segment.rule_applied` with counts only (never the repo list, matching the bulk route's reasoning at src/app/api/org/segments/[id]/repos/bulk/route.ts:35) and register the action in src/features/admin/audit/auditActions.ts.
- Turn the auto-add control into "define rule": it saves the rule and then applies it once, so the existing gesture still ends in tagged repos. Keep the manual chips untouched.
- Render the drift: a new SegmentRuleRow.tsx (client, Apply button) shown from SegmentCard.tsx when a rule exists, reading the pure drift result. Both files stay well under the 200-LOC features cap.
- Update docs/features/org-dashboard/org-intelligence.md (segments are now declared, with ownership and drift) and docs/features/data/data-model.md (two new columns).

## Expected impact
An org that organizes its fleet by language or team stops silently reporting on last month's fleet: a new repo joins its segment, segment-scoped scans and cadence writes hit the right repos, and when the operator has not applied yet the screen says how many repos are missing instead of looking complete. Measured by the drift count readable on the Segments view and by the audit row's added/removed counts. What could break: a careless convergence deleting hand-made tags, which is exactly what the `source` column and acceptance case 3 exist to forbid.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a user-declared slice of the fleet converges to its declaration instead of freezing on the day it was created, without a rule ever reaping a human's tag.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - the acceptance cases as tests (segmentRule.test.ts for the pure drift/ownership rules, segments.test.ts for applySegmentRule, route.test.ts for the gate and audit), red before, green after.
Result: better
Gate: architecture

## Summary
The segment comparison is two dots per row. A segment of 20 repos and a segment of 2 look identical, and a 14-point gap on a dimension names no repo and offers no action, although the rollup it was averaged from holds every repo's per-dimension score (src/lib/db/segments.ts:370).

## Description
compareSegments returns means and only means (src/lib/db/segments.ts:464, shape at src/lib/db/segments.ts:297). SegmentsComparePanel draws them as a dumbbell: one filled mark, one hollow mark, a delta (src/features/standing/repositories/SegmentDumbbell.tsx:72, dimension card at src/features/standing/repositories/SegmentsComparePanel.tsx:122). The reader learns that "Platform trails Legacy by 14 on Testing" and then has to leave: back to the Repositories tab, set `?segment=`, sort, and guess which repos drag the mean - the data is one tab away from the question it answers.

This is not an unnoticed gap; it is a recorded one. src/features/standing/repositories/segmentViz.ts:5 explains that a paired row was the honest drawing BECAUSE only means were available, and src/features/standing/repositories/segmentViz.ts:8 escalates the fix by name: "a real distribution per segment needs `compareSegments` to return the per-repo scores it already reads, and that is `src/lib/db`'s call to make." This card adopts that escalation, which is why its first move is in the db layer and not in the chart.

The producer is already holding the rows. summarizeScopedRepos (src/lib/db/segments.ts:366) reduces the rollup's repo rows and reads r.latest.dims per repo (src/lib/db/segments.ts:370) on its way to an average, then drops them. Meanwhile the comparison pays for its own data twice over: two summarizeSegment calls (src/lib/db/segments.ts:481) each run a scoped getOrgRollup whose own header documents that the whole scan history crosses the wire (src/lib/db/org-rollup.ts:731), on a page that already ran one unscoped rollup (src/lib/db/segments.ts:406). So the fix is cheaper than the status quo: partition the ONE rollup by the membership map (the move listSegmentSummaries already makes, and the one tech-groups made for stacks at src/lib/db/tech-groups.ts:132), keep the per-repo points on each side, and delete the last caller of summarizeScopedRollup (src/lib/db/tech-groups.ts:161 notes segments are the only one left).

The registry rule that governs the drawing, resolved through ../ai-registry/knowledge/software-engineering/index.json: `peer-benchmarking`'s technique `population-vs-scalar-ranking` - "both sides must be the same kind of thing" - plus its `basis-disclosure`. Honouring it is what keeps the new chart honest: the mean mark stays labelled a mean, the item marks stay labelled items, every side prints the n it rests on, and a one-repo "mean" says so (acceptance 6 and 7). `measurement-honesty` supplies the rule this surface already follows and must not lose: an absent score is a gap, never a 0 (src/lib/db/segments.ts:280, src/features/standing/repositories/SegmentDumbbell.tsx:90).

Fixed looks like: each side of the comparison carries its repo points; the headline and dimension rows draw a strip of item marks with the mean marked on it; and a dimension where one side trails expands into that side's repos ranked worst-first on THAT dimension, each with its report link and, when the repo is watched, the existing one-click Rescan (src/features/standing/repositories/RepoRescanButton.tsx:18). The gap stops being a readout and becomes the start of the work.

## Flow
- Move the comparison half of src/lib/db/segments.ts into src/lib/db/segments-compare.ts and keep segments.ts as a re-export barrel (the src/lib/db/org.ts and src/lib/db/scans.ts pattern AGENTS.md names), so no call site or db/index.ts consumer changes shape.
- Add `points: { fullName: string; overall: number; dims: { dimId: string; score: number }[] }[]` to the summary/comparison sides, produced inside summarizeScopedRepos from the rows it already walks. No Date crosses the boundary, so src/lib/db/wire-safe-dates.test.ts stays satisfied.
- Rewrite compareSegments to take one rollup plus the membership map and reduce both sides in memory (reusing summarizeScopedRepos), then delete summarizeScopedRollup and summarizeSegment and drop their export from src/lib/db/index.ts. Tests for the one-read claim and the unchanged means go in first.
- Extend src/features/standing/repositories/segmentViz.ts with distribution rows (items + mean per side, nulls preserved) and delete the "the data cannot support a distribution" note it is now wrong about; extend segmentViz.test.ts alongside.
- New SegmentDistribution.tsx: server-safe SVG strip per metric row (items as small marks, the mean as the labelled mark, n printed), with the sr-only table SegmentDumbbell already models.
- New SegmentGapLaggards.tsx: the expanded dimension's worst-first repo list for the trailing side, report link per row, RepoRescanButton for watched repos only. SegmentsComparePanel.tsx orchestrates and stays under the 200-LOC features cap by holding no list markup itself.
- Thread the watched set and the points through SegmentsSection.tsx and SegmentsSection.v2.tsx (both already fetch listWatchedRepos at src/features/standing/repositories/SegmentsSection.tsx:43), then update docs/features/org-dashboard/org-intelligence.md.

## Expected impact
An engineering leader comparing two slices sees the SHAPE of each (a tight cluster versus one repo dragging a mean of three) and can act on the gap in place - open the worst repo's report or rescan it - instead of re-deriving the set on another tab. Measurable as the removal of two full fleet rollups per Segments view (acceptance 2) and as expand-then-act events on the dimension rows. What could break: a wide segment drawing dozens of overlapping marks, which is why the strip caps and summarises the tail rather than plotting unbounded marks.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a segment comparison becomes two populations you can interrogate and act on, for one fleet read instead of three.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - the acceptance cases as tests (segments.test.ts for points, the single-read spy and the unchanged means; segmentViz.test.ts for the distribution rows and null handling; a dom test for the expand/laggard/rescan rules), red before, green after.
Result: better
Gate: contract

## Summary
/api/scan and /api/scan/stream each hand-sequence the same post-gate scan run (coordinate parse, scope resolve, head and cache lookup, cached return, coalesce, classify, refund, cache and persist), and the copies have already drifted: the stream route parses GitHub coordinates only (`src/app/api/scan/stream/route.ts:67`) so the live scan path cannot scan the GitLab repos the form, the docs and /api/scan all accept, and it has no error salvage.

## Description
The pre-scan gates were already single-sourced into `src/lib/scan-gates.ts` and the persist guards into `src/lib/scan-finalize.ts`, for a reason that file states plainly: "Both routes ran byte-identical copies of the burst rate limiter ... a fix to one silently missed the other" (`src/lib/scan-gates.ts:2-4`), and the stream route once ran paid inference with no credit meter at all (`src/lib/scan-gates.ts:133-137`). What was never extracted is the SEQUENCE between those helpers, so the routes still own ~150 lines each of identical ordering, and the agreement is held by prose plus a route-source test (`src/app/api/scan/gate-order.test.ts:1-11`).

The drift that is live today: the JSON route resolves a forge coordinate (`src/app/api/scan/route.ts:81`, with `ghParsed` for the GitHub-keyed side paths and `repoIdentity` for persistence), while the stream route calls `parseRepoUrl` (`src/app/api/scan/stream/route.ts:67`) and 400s with GitHub-only copy (`:73`). The scan form deliberately accepts GitLab and emits `gitlab:group/project` (`src/components/scan/normalizeScanRepo.ts:44`, error copy at `src/components/ScanForm.tsx:117`), pushes it to /report (`src/components/ScanForm.tsx:143`), and /report scans over the stream (`src/components/report/useReportScan.ts:208`). So the product's front door offers a scan it cannot run, and `docs/features/scanning/scan.md:3` asserts the capability. Second drift: the any-commit error salvage (`src/app/api/scan/route.ts:385-388`) exists only on the JSON route, so a transient GitHub failure five minutes into a live scan gives the user an error where the other endpoint would have served last week's report. Third: a coalesce joiner refunds the credit on the stream (`src/app/api/scan/stream/route.ts:311-312`) and only the quota on the JSON route (`src/app/api/scan/route.ts:397`); that is harmless today only because coalescing is confined to the unmetered anonymous path, an invariant nothing pins.

The governing standard is `codebase-scanning`'s first wall, sensor-pipeline: a scan is a pipeline whose "stage boundaries are where its reliability lives", to be defended "as interfaces, not as an implementation accident", with persistence as the stage that makes the sweep longitudinal. Here the terminal stages live twice, in two HTTP handlers. Fixed looks like: `src/lib/scan-lifecycle.ts` owns the run from coordinate to persisted report, parameterized by a protocol adapter (how to deliver a cached hit, a progress frame, a result, an error) and by the per-route gate placement the routes legitimately differ on (`src/lib/scan-gates.ts:20-24`); the two routes become thin adapters.

Note on the registry row: the recorded `codebase-scanning` deviation (governance/posture/exposure `.catch(() => null)` with score-bearing folds) is largely CLOSED in this tree and its verdict is STALE - `src/lib/scan-ingest.ts:126-131` is the one shared sensor recorder, `src/lib/scan-score-input.ts:141` threads it into the D9 battery, and `src/lib/scoring/gate.ts:222` skips criteria a failed sensor could have refuted. Neither card re-proposes it.

## Flow
- Write the failing parity test first: one table over { cached hit, join, degrade, dedup, throw, abort } x { quota, credit }, driven against both entry points.
- Extract `runScanLifecycle(input, adapter)` into `src/lib/scan-lifecycle.ts`: coordinate (via `parseForgeUrl`, carrying the `ghParsed` / `repoIdentity` split), scope resolve, head and cache lookup, scoped lookup, cached return, coalesce, classify, refund ledger, cacheAndPersist, salvage-on-failure.
- Make the refund ledger explicit (one object with `onCacheHit`, `onJoin`, `onDegrade`, `onDedup`, `onFailure`) instead of six hand-placed awaits per route.
- Rewrite /api/scan as the JSON adapter (keeping its gate placement after the free cache/peek returns, and its private-scan wall above the limiter).
- Rewrite /api/scan/stream as the SSE adapter (frames, heartbeat, notify, persisted frame), now forge-capable and salvage-capable by construction.
- Update `context-map.json` (declare `src/lib/scan-lifecycle.ts`) and `docs/features/scanning/scan.md` (the GitLab-on-stream capability becomes true; the "thin wrappers" claim at line 12 becomes accurate).

## Expected impact
A user pasting a GitLab repo into the product's front door gets a scan instead of "Enter a valid GitHub repository URL", and a live scan that hits a transient GitHub failure lands on the last saved report instead of a dead end. Measured by the two divergence acceptance cases plus the parity table (red before, green after) and by the deletion of ~300 duplicated lines from the two routes. What could break: this is the money path - a mis-sequenced refund either mints or burns a credit, so the parity table must be written before the extraction and the credit gate must stay the last gate on both routes.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience | quality - one sequence for one run, so a fix to the scan lifecycle cannot land on one entry point only, and two live divergences (forge blindness, no salvage) close with it.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases as vitest cases over both route handlers plus the new lifecycle module, red before, green after.
Result: better
Gate: architecture

A detached run that is still in flight when the function's duration budget ends records a scan failure outcome (recordScanFailure) and refunds, rather than vanishing with the viewer told an email is coming.
The email is dispatched exactly once when the client reconnects and also receives the result frame (no double send), keyed on the run, not on the connection.

## Summary
The product offers "Email me when it's done (scans take a few minutes)" (`src/components/scan/NotifyToggle.tsx:75`), but closing the tab aborts the scan: the pipeline's abort signal is the client connection (`src/app/api/scan/stream/route.ts:309`), the catch refunds and unwinds (`:401-402`), and the email lives after the result frame inside the stream (`:385-392`). The one feature whose entire purpose is not waiting on the tab only works if you wait on the tab.

## Description
A scan is a multi-minute job: the component's own header says so (`src/components/scan/NotifyToggle.tsx:3-5`), and the signed-out nudge sells sign-in on it (`:43-44`). Yet the run is owned by the HTTP request. `request.signal` is threaded into `scanRepository` (`src/app/api/scan/stream/route.ts:309`), `cancel()` fires on disconnect (`:433-436`), and the coalesce layer aborts the shared run as soon as the last connected caller leaves (`src/lib/cache.ts:332`). So a user who checks the box and closes the tab gets: no report, no persisted row, no email, and a refunded slot they never learn about. A user who returns two minutes later starts a second full scan from zero.

This is the clause `background-jobs` / `job-progress-and-cancellation` names as the one most often skipped: "The observer is not the owner. A viewer navigating away, a window closing, a client restarting - none of these touch the job", and re-attachment is a snapshot plus a subscribe rather than events-since-mount. Ascent has the subscribe half already (`coalesceScan` fans frames to joiners and replays the last frame, `src/lib/cache.ts:292-322`) and even the "Joining a scan already in progress" frame; what is missing is an owner that outlives the connection.

Fixed looks like a detachable run. When the viewer opted into notify (which already requires a signed-in account with a verified address, so the detached run is attributable and the abuse surface is the same one the burst limiter and the monthly quota already bound), the scan is owned by a KEEPER rather than by the connection: the coalesce entry holds a non-leaving waiter, the scan gets its own deadline-bound signal instead of `request.signal`, and the finalization (classify, cache and persist, email, outcome tally) is handed to `after()` - the shape `src/app/api/app/webhook/route.ts:663` already runs a full clientless scan in. The disconnect then stops the SSE writes and nothing else, and a viewer who comes back re-attaches to the live run instead of paying for a second one. The refund rules invert for a detached run only: the slot and the credit stand because the scan will deliver, and they are refunded on the detached run's own failure, abort or degrade, so every exit still converges on one finalization.

## Flow
- Add a keeper to `coalesceScan`: an entry may be held by a non-connection owner, so `waiters <= 0` no longer aborts it, and the keeper releases on the run's own settle.
- Give the detached scan its own AbortController bounded by the invocation deadline, and stop passing `request.signal` on that branch.
- Move the finalization (classify -> refund ledger -> cacheAndPersist -> notify email -> outcome tally) behind one function the connected path and the `after()` path both call, so an exit cannot skip it; guard the email on the run, not on the connection, so a reconnected viewer cannot trigger a second send.
- Invert the refund rule for a detached run: no refund on disconnect; refund on the detached run's failure, deadline abort or degrade-to-mock.
- Client: NotifyToggle says the tab can be closed; useReportScan shows a detached state on navigate-away and, on return, re-attaches through the existing peek then stream join.
- Update `docs/features/scanning/scan.md` (the disconnect sentence at line 138, and the notify section) in the same change.

## Expected impact
The users most likely to abandon the product - first-timers facing a multi-minute wait - can check a box, leave, and get the report by email, which is what the UI already promises. Measured by: a detached run completes and mails after a disconnect (acceptance 1), and a return visit during a live run costs zero extra ingest and zero extra inference (acceptance 4, countable as one scan row and one LLM call per commit). What could break: abort-on-disconnect is deliberate cost control, so a detached run keeps spending GitHub rate limit and LLM budget for a viewer who is gone. It is confined to the authenticated notify opt-in, bounded by the same burst limiter and monthly quota, and bounded again by the invocation deadline; a detached run that outlives the deadline must report a failure rather than silence.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the "email me when it's done" opt-in delivers without the tab staying open, and a returning viewer rejoins the live scan instead of restarting it.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - the acceptance cases as vitest cases over the stream route (disconnect driven by aborting the request signal mid-scan) and over coalesceScan's keeper, red before, green after.
Result: better
Gate: direction (policy-loosen: a notify-opted scan deliberately keeps spending after the client disconnects, where today every disconnect refunds and stops)
runner_up: Turn the scan's reliability caveats into an actionable "what this scan could not see" panel on the live scan surface: report.warnings and report.sensorFailures are prose and an id list today (src/lib/scan-compose.ts:214-249), so the user reads that governance was unreadable but is offered no action; pair each entry with the one fix (sign in, install the App, re-run with a token) and a re-run that keeps the scope.
coordinator_revision: Build on card 4's coalesceScan entry instead of adding a second mechanism: the notify opt-in sets a detached flag on the SAME inflight entry that disables card 4's linger expiry, so cache.ts gains one lifecycle rather than a linger window and a keeper; the coordinator sequences this card after card 4 lands and the builder rebases on it.

## Summary
The Skills Library has four write doors and each re-decides the plan/personal entitlement itself: create (src/app/api/org/skills/route.ts:64), promote (promote/route.ts:47), edit (`[id]`/route.ts:34) and push (push/route.ts:40). Push calls a different predicate and skips the cap, and `pushOrgSkill` cannot see that a name is archived (src/lib/db/org-skills.ts:579), so a push to an archived name reports success and writes a row nobody can see.

## Description
The entitlement is three facts: does the plan allow the library, is this a personal workspace on the free path, and is the personal cap reached. Three of the four doors spell those out inline (src/app/api/org/skills/route.ts:64 and :67; promote/route.ts:47 and :50; `[id]`/route.ts:34, cap deliberately absent). The fourth gates on `planAllowsSkillsLibrary` directly (push/route.ts:40) and never consults the cap. The divergence IS intended - docs/features/org-knowledge/skills.md:232 declares that the CLI/CI push path does not extend the personal free tier - but it is declared in prose beside four hand-copied call sites, which makes a deliberate exception indistinguishable from drift the day a fifth door is added. The registry's `plan-entitlements` technique `capability-gate-predicates` (use_when: "gating a feature behind a plan", laws `one-validation-door`, `failure-not-empty-success`) asks for one pure predicate returning an ENUMERATED decision, not a boolean per route; `tier-model-single-source` asks for the tier rule in one place. Today every refusal collapses to the same string ("The Skills Library is a Team-plan feature." at route.ts:65, promote/route.ts:49, `[id]`/route.ts:35, push/route.ts:41), so a CLI cannot tell "your plan" from "this door is Team-only for personal workspaces" from "you are at 10 of 10".

The same seam carries a live defect. `pushOrgSkill` looks a skill up by `where: { orgId, name }` with no `archived` filter (src/lib/db/org-skills.ts:579-582), while `listOrgSkills` (:168) and `listOrgSkillManifest` (:540) both filter `archived: false`. So pushing a name an admin archived takes the update branch: 200 `updated`, version bumped, content replaced - and the skill appears in no list, no manifest and no tab. The CLI records a version the server will never offer it again. `invariant-placement`'s `placement-precedes-gate` is the shape of the fix: the archived state must be read where the row is resolved, not hoped for at the call site.

Fixed looks like `src/lib/org/skill-write-gate.ts`: a closed `SkillWriteDoor` union (create | edit | promote | push), one `Record` of door rules (does the personal path apply, does the cap apply), and `skillWriteDecision(org, door)` returning `{ allowed, decision, limit?, remaining? }`. Each route calls it once and maps the decision to its status and message. The push exception becomes a row in that table, pinned by a test over doors x tier, and `pushOrgSkill` grows an archived branch that returns a named `archived` status instead of writing in the dark.

## Flow
- Write `src/lib/org/skill-write-gate.ts`: the door union, the rule table, the enumerated decision, and a thin `deniedResponse(decision)` mapper for the routes.
- Table test first (`skill-write-gate.test.ts`): doors x (plan free/team) x (kind org/personal) x (live count below/at cap), asserting one decision per cell. Red before the module exists.
- Replace the inline chain in create, promote and edit with the single call; keep each route's existing status codes for the decisions they already return.

title: Retire sweep: act on the prune candidates the library already computes
acceptance: A library of 3 abandoned + 2 unused + 4 unmeasured skills renders a sweep listing exactly the 3 abandoned ids; the other 6 are absent and the panel states in one line that never-used and never-measured skills are not offered (isPruneCandidate is the only selector).
A library with zero abandoned skills renders no sweep panel at all (no empty card).

Each candidate row shows its blast radius from data the tab already holds: adopted repo count (adoption[id].adoptedRepos.length), last use date and days since (usage[id].lastUsedAt / daysSinceUse), and the window it was judged against (usage[id].windowDays). A candidate with 2 adoptions reads "2 repos recorded this"; a candidate with 0 reads "no repo recorded this".

A registry-origin candidate (skill.origin === "registry") is listed as not retirable with its reason (the next index pass would restore it), and POST /api/org/skills/retire with such an id refuses that id and names it in { skipped }.

POST /api/org/skills/retire { org, ids } as an admin archives exactly those ids and returns { retired: n, skipped: [] }; the same call as a non-admin member returns 403 and archives nothing; an id belonging to another org is skipped, not archived, and n excludes it.

The number the confirm step shows equals response.retired, and when they differ the panel shows the difference instead of the optimistic number (preview and execution share skillRetireModel's candidate set).

POST /api/org/skills/retire { org, ids, restore: true } right after a sweep sets archived back to false for those ids and the rows reappear in the list on the next refresh; the undo control is offered for the duration of the panel's session.

Each retired id writes one org_skill.archived audit row carrying { via: "sweep" }, and a restore writes org_skill.updated with { archived: false } (both action values already exist in src/features/admin/audit/auditActions.ts:111-112, so no new action is registered).

body:
## Summary
The library computes exactly which skills are honest prune candidates - `isPruneCandidate` at src/lib/org/skill-usage.ts:90, counted as `UsageSummary.abandoned` at :420 - and no surface acts on it. The only retire affordance is a per-row `archive` text link (src/features/shared/skills/SkillCardActions.tsx:49) reached by expanding one row at a time, with no confirmation, no blast radius and no undo.

## Description
The dormancy model in `skill-usage.ts` is unusually careful: `dormant` is split into `abandoned` (tried, then silence), `unused` (a discovery problem) and `unmeasured` (the pathway never spoke), and only `abandoned` may be pruned (:90, and the doc restates it at docs/features/org-knowledge/skills.md:406). That judgement reaches the user as paint only: `SkillDormancyBadge` colours it, `skillSceneModel.ts:99` counts it, and the sole action is the per-row `archive` link. `isPruneCandidate` has no caller outside its own module and test (grep: src/lib/org/skill-usage.ts, src/lib/org/skill-usage.test.ts only). So a librarian with nine quiet skills is told "three of these are findings" and must then expand nine rows, remember which three, and click a link that fires DELETE immediately (src/features/shared/skills/useSkillsLibrary.ts:66) with no statement of what it costs and no way back in the UI.

That is the gap the registry's `entity-lifecycle` techniques are about. `blast-radius-computation` (use_when: "designing what a destructive confirmation shows", "users click through every confirm dialog") requires the dependants to be enumerated and shown BEFORE the ask, with preview and execution sharing one implementation; today the dependants exist on the client already (`adoption[id].adoptedRepos`, SkillCard.tsx:44) and are simply never shown at the moment of archiving. `bulk-deletion-rails` requires a named scope, a preserved core, a preview and accounting; the preserved core here is handed to us by the model - `unused` and `unmeasured` are never eligible, and a registry-origin row is not ours to retire (SkillCardActions.tsx:46-48 already says so for the single case). `archive-restore-semantics` is why undo is cheap: archive is already a reversible flag (src/lib/db/org-skills.ts:274).

Fixed looks like one review-then-retire panel above the table, present only when the library has at least one `abandoned` skill: the candidates with their last use, their judged window and the repos that recorded them, a scope sentence naming the predicate, a confirm that quotes the count, and one undo. Behind it a single admin-gated `POST /api/org/skills/retire { org, ids, restore? }` that re-derives eligibility server-side (so a forged id, a cross-tenant id or a registry-origin id is skipped and named, not archived) and audits each row with the existing `org_skill.archived` action.

## Flow
- `skillRetireModel.ts` (pure, no JSX): candidate selection over `isPruneCandidate`, the per-candidate blast-radius row (adoptions, last use, days since, window, origin), the refusal reasons for the ineligible, and the scope sentence. Tested first.
- `POST /api/org/skills/retire`: admin gate (mirroring `[id]` DELETE at src/app/api/org/skills/[id]/route.ts:119-126), re-derive eligibility from the server's own usage read, archive the eligible, return `{ retired, skipped: [{ id, reason }] }`, audit per row. `restore: true` flips `archived` back through the same door.
- `SkillRetireSweep.tsx` ("use client"): the list, the confirm quoting the count, the result line, the undo. Under the 200-LOC features cap; any overflow extracts a co-located row component.
- Wire the retire/restore mutation into `useSkillsLibrary.ts` (93 lines today, so the cap holds) and mount the panel in both `SkillsPanel.tsx` and `SkillsPanel.v2.tsx`.
- Update docs/features/org-knowledge/skills.md: the surface section, the route table near :594, and the prune-candidate paragraph at :406 which currently ends at the classification.

## Expected impact
The org librarian stops reading a verdict they cannot act on: nine expansions and a blind click become one reviewed sweep that states what each retirement costs and can be undone. Measured by the acceptance cases plus the fact that a retirement now leaves an audit row naming its route (`via: "sweep"`), so the sweep's use is countable. What could break: a batch archive is destructive-adjacent, so a bug could hide skills that were merely never measured - the server re-derives eligibility rather than trusting the posted ids, and the restore path is in the same change.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the library's own prune verdict becomes a reviewable, reversible action instead of a colour.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases written as tests in skillRetireModel.test.ts, SkillRetireSweep.dom.test.tsx and retire/route.test.ts, red before, green after
Result: better
Gate: contract
